report.clinical_summary: Patient with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia experiencing persistent fatigue and night sweats that significantly disrupt daily life. Not currently on medication; following 'watch and wait' approach. Patient feels uncertain about future timeline, has very little personal control, and is emotionally affected with anxiety and feeling overwhelmed. Trusts medical team's judgment and approach.

evidence.quote: my illness is taking a toll on me. Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia has really disrupted my life
even getting out of bed in the morning is a struggle. Simple tasks take a lot more effort than they should
I don't remember feeling this uncomfortable while sleeping for years now
it's taking a real toll on me and my life
It feels invasive and overwhelming to have something so disruptive just linger within me without any clear end in sight

consequences.reasoning: Patient describes significant disruption to daily life - getting out of bed is a struggle, simple tasks take much more effort, they have persistent night sweats that are uncomfortable, and they feel the illness has 'taken over every aspect of my life'. They've had to adapt their life substantially.

evidence.quote: it feels like there's no end in sight

But then there's another part of me that holds onto hope that new treatments will come along and make a difference

timeline.reasoning: Patient expresses significant uncertainty about the future timeline. They fear it might be for years or the rest of their life, but also hold onto hope for improvement. They don't have a clear expectation.
